score.product: AUTOMATED INSULIN DOSING DEVICE SYSTEM, SINGLE HORMONAL CONTROL
score.rationale: CRITICAL: This is pure indication confounding. Automated insulin delivery systems (closed-loop pumps) are prescribed to manage diabetes and prevent hyperglycemia; hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) is the *target condition's opposite extreme* and a known, labeled risk of insulin therapy itself. The signal reflects the device's normal operation and occasional overcorrection, not a novel injury. Despite massive case count (5666) and Class III PMA status, this is not a failure-to-warn but an inherent treatment risk. Zero viability.

preemption_flag.note: AUTOMATED INSULIN DOSING DEVICE SYSTEM, SINGLE HORMONAL CONTROL is a PMA (Class III) device. Riegel v. Medtronic preempts state design-defect and failure-to-warn claims on PMA devices; viability is downweighted. Parallel claims (manufacturing defect / violation of the device's own FDA-approved requirements, failure to report to FDA) survive preemption — assess those before passing.

score.rationale: This is a classic indication-confounding artifact. Leflunomide is prescribed for rheumatoid arthritis; anti-CCP antibody positivity is a diagnostic marker and prognostic indicator of RA, not an injury caused by the drug. The reports reflect patients with active/severe RA (the condition being treated), not a new adverse event. The PRR collapse to zero in 2026Q2 confirms this is a reporting artifact. There is no duty to warn that a drug may fail to treat—or that treated patients still have—the disease it targets. Score viability zero and pass immediately.
